lines.li: [us] Is {THEN} over at home?
[them] It's over, though the fields will take a while to forgive it.
[us] I'm glad it's behind you.
[them] So are we, and we still watch the sky every morning.
[us] Any rain at home yet?
[them] Not enough to speak of, and the wells are lower every week.
[us] I'm sorry, I hope it turns soon.
[us] Are your herds well again?
[them] What's left of them, and the smoke fires are out at last.
[us] That's something.
[them] It's a start, and we'll build them back.
[us] Is {THEN} still in your herds?
[them] Still, and we've stopped counting what it's taken.
[us] I'm sorry, truly.
[us] Is it still bitter at home, with {THEN}?
[them,their:tribal] Still, and we sleep in one long house to save the wood.
[them] Still, and the woodpiles are getting short.
[us] I hope it breaks soon.
[us] Is {THEN} still unwell, after all this time?
[them] Still, and we've stopped expecting it to change.
[us] Tell them they're in our thoughts.
[us] How are things at home since {THEN} died?
[them] Quieter, and some nights someone still sets a place for them.
[us] That's a kind thing to do.
[them] It's what we do, until we don't need to.
[us] Is {THEN} still in your hills?
[them] Gone, one way or another, and the hills feel emptier for it.
[us] I hope it was the gentle way.
[them] So do I, and I'd rather not ask.
[them] {THEN} is still wandering our hills, slow as ever.
[us] Nobody's gone after it?
[them] Nobody yet, and the elders mean to keep it that way.
[us] Remember {THEN}, that we talked about?
[them] Gone from the sky, and the arguing about what it meant has only got louder.
[us] Did anything come of it?
[them] Nothing anyone agrees on, which is how you know it was a proper omen.
[them] {THEN} is finished, you'll be glad to hear.
[us] Glad isn't quite the word.
[them] No, but it'll do for now.
[us] Is {THEN} still riding?
[them] Still, and every raid brings it more riders.
[us] Then keep to the daylight on your way home.
[us] How did {THEN} go, in the end?
[them] Everyone went home grumbling, which means it was probably fair.
[us] That's one way to tell.
[us] Is {THEN} over, then?
[them] Over, swept up, and already argued about for a year to come.
[us] Who won the cooking?
[them] Depends who you ask, and everyone will tell you it was them.
[us] Any change with {THEN} since we talked?
[them] Not much, it goes on, and we go on with it.
[us] That's all anyone can do.
[us] Last time you spoke of the war with {THEN}, how goes it now?
[them,war:losing] Badly, we've fewer towns than when it started.
[them,war:winning] Better, they've lost ground since it began.
[them,!war:losing,!war:winning] The same, which is its own kind of bad.
[us] I'll keep hoping for you.
[us] Is the peace with {THEN} holding?
[them] Holding, and every month it holds, people breathe a little easier.
[us] Long may it last.
[them] The peace with {THEN} didn't hold, we're at war again.
[us] I'm sorry, after all that.
[them,their:tribal] The spears came off the wall faster than they went up.
[them] So am I, it was good while it lasted.
[them] You asked about {THEN} once, well, {NOW} leads us now.
[us] I hadn't heard.
[them] Few have, and we're all still getting used to it.
[us] I hope {NOW} does well by you.
[them,their:tribal] The elders are watching, and so are the spirits.
[them] So do we, and we'll know soon enough.
[us] Is {THEN} still leading your people?
[them] Still, and nobody expects that to change soon.
[us] Steady hands, then.
[them] Steady, or stubborn, depending on who you ask.
[us] Is {THEN} still at the head of things in {TOWN}?
[them] Still, and still listening to everyone and agreeing with no one.
[us] That sounds like leading, all right.
[us] How is {THEN}?
[them] {THEN} is gone, I'm sorry to say.
[us] I'm sorry, I liked hearing about them.
[them] They'd have liked that, being talked about by strangers.
[us] Is {THEN} still keeping busy?
[them] Busier than ever, and still telling everyone so.
[us] Give them our regards again.
[us] Is {THEN} still out there near {TOWN}?
[them] Still there, and still giving people bad dreams.
[us] Somebody will deal with it one day.
[them] You saw {THEN} through, and people at home were glad to hear it.
[us] It was worth doing.
[them,their:tribal] The elders say your name a little warmer now.
[them] It'll be remembered, believe me.
[us] {THEN} didn't go the way we wanted.
[them] I heard, and so did everyone at home.
[us] We'll do better next time.
[them] I hope so, for both our sakes.
[them] Whatever became of {THEN}?
[us] It's finished, one way and another.
[them] Fair enough, they don't all end neatly.
[them] Still at {THEN}, are you?
[us] Still, it's taking longer than we hoped.
[them] Most things worth doing do.
[us] Are you any closer to what you hoped for when we last talked?
[them] A step or two, and I haven't given up on it.
[us] Good, don't.
[us] Still busy with your {THEIRSKILL}?
[them] Busier than ever, and better at it, I like to think.
[us] I'll take your word for it.
[us] Did trade pick up, after last time?
[them,rich] Here, it always does.
[them] Up and down, the way it always is.
[us] Then let's make today an up.
[them] I told them about you in {TOWN}, the way I said I would.
[us] And what did they say?
[them] That I talk too much, which is fair.
[us] Fair, but we don't mind.
[us] How's that little one of yours, {THEIRCHILD}?
[them] Bigger and louder every time I come home.
[us] That's how it should be.
[us] Is {THEIRSPOUSE} keeping well?
[them] Well, and asking when I'll stay home for good.
[us] And will you?
[them] One day, maybe, but not yet.
[us] Still sure about {THEIRFAITH}?
[them] Surer than ever, and you're still welcome to try me.
[us] I'll leave that to the preachers.
[them] I know the way here by heart now.
[us] Then you've no excuse not to come more often.
[them] I'll think of one.
